_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: Loads from IndexedDB show a status, loads from memory render at once, and the HUD reports both. The performance-hud flag is on. The conversation {{ID}} (slug {{CSLUG}}) is a medium /debug/loremipsum conversation of exactly {{COUNT}} messages. window.__shelleyLoadingStatuses lists, for the current page, each text the loading status (".conversation-loading") showed, as {text, messageElements} with the number of [data-testid="message"] elements at that moment. Call "mark" notes where the browser's requests are; call "full loads" returns how many full loads of the conversation (GET /api/conversation/{{ID}} without last_sequence_id) the browser has made since. "The HUD" is the ".perf-hud" element; "the latest load" is window.__shelleyPerf.loads().at(-1). 1. Navigate to /c/{{ID}}. 2. The element with data-testid "message-input" should be visible (allow 30s), and the first element with data-testid "message" too (allow 30s). 3. Wait until IndexedDB has the whole history: eval this until it returns true (allow 30s): (async () => { const db = await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { const req = indexedDB.open('shelley-messages'); req.onsuccess = () => resolve(req.result); req.onerror = () => reject(req.error); }); try { if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains('conversation_meta')) return false; const row = await new Promise((resolve) => { const get = db.transaction('conversation_meta', 'readonly').objectStore('conversation_meta').get('{{ID}}'); get.onsuccess = () => resolve(get.result); get.onerror = () => resolve(undefined); }); return !!(row && row.has_full_history); } finally { db.close(); } })(). 4. Call "mark"; it returns "marked". 5. Reload. 6. The first element with data-testid "message" should be visible (allow 30s). 7. Eval window.__shelleyLoadingStatuses.some((s) => s.text.includes('{{STATUS}}') && s.messageElements === 0): it must return true (the status named the message count while no message was mounted yet). 8. There should be exactly 0 ".conversation-loading" elements (allow 30s). 9. Call "full loads": it must return exactly "0" (the history came from IndexedDB). 10. Eval (() => { const l = window.__shelleyPerf.loads().at(-1); return !!l && l.conversationId === '{{ID}}' && l.source === 'indexeddb' && l.messages === {{COUNT}} && l.totalMs > 0 && l.renderMs > 0; })(): true. 11. The HUD's first ".perf-hud-load" should contain "IndexedDB" (allow 5s). 12. The expanded HUD overlays the drawer, so collapse it: click the HUD's ".perf-hud-title". 13. Eval document.querySelector('.perf-hud').classList.contains('collapsed') until it returns true. 14. In one eval without "expect", empty the list: window.__shelleyLoadingStatuses.length = 0. 15. Start a new conversation from the header: click the ".header" button named exactly "New Conversation" (role "button"; if the header does not show it, click the button named exactly "More options", then the button named exactly "New Conversation" in ".chat-overflow-popover"). 16. The URL should end in /new (assert_url, exact path "/new"). 17. Open the conversation list: on a phone, click the button with aria-label "Open conversations" and ".drawer.open" should be visible (on a wide screen, click the button with aria-label "Expand sidebar" if it shows instead). 18. "The row" is the element inside a ".conversation-title" whose text is exactly "{{CSLUG}}" (within ".conversation-title", selector "*", has_text "{{CSLUG}}", exact). Scroll it into view if needed, and it should then be in the viewport (assert_in_viewport). 19. Click the row. 20. The first element with data-testid "message" should be visible (allow 30s). 21. Eval JSON.stringify(window.__shelleyLoadingStatuses): exactly "[]" (a memory hit renders in the switch's own flush: no loading status). 22. Eval (() => { const l = window.__shelleyPerf.loads().at(-1); return !!l && l.conversationId === '{{ID}}' && l.source === 'memory' && l.messages === {{COUNT}}; })() until it returns true (the load is recorded once rendered, which can trail the first message showing). 23. Click the HUD's ".perf-hud-title" to expand it. 24. The HUD's first ".perf-hud-load" should contain "Memory".
